options.labelReason: Seven law courses provide the core. Political institutions, ethics, rhetoric and historical research support comparative analysis and argumentation.
options.concept: Compare legal systems and study how constitutional, private, criminal, European and international law work. Use political science and philosophy to examine institutions and legal reasoning, and develop argumentation and research skills.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes dependent law courses. Introductory rhetoric precedes advanced persuasion and public speaking. Comparative Politics precedes European Union Politics.

options.label: Law, Justice and Social Change
options.labelReason: Law and human rights are studied alongside sociology, social movements, ethics, history and public economics.

options.distinctness: The plans share 14 courses. This plan adds ten courses in sociology, historical inequality, AI ethics, media and race, and methods and public economics. The closest plan gives greater weight to private law, EU institutions, international relations and argumentation.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes dependent law courses. Introductory and modern sociology precede advanced social theory. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Public Economics.

analysis: The closest plan combines comparative public and private law with criminal, international and EU law. The gateway directly supports introductory case briefing and legal reasoning. Private law includes comparative contract research and simulated mediation. Criminal law teaches liability and gives students a simulated legal-aid clinic with written advice and oral argument. EU law covers legal sources, competences, remedies and free movement. Comparative Constitutional Law offers genuine introductory administrative-law content. UCR does not reproduce Maastricht’s separate criminal procedure course or its legal skills and research sequence. The second plan connects legal rights and public law to sociology, social movements, media, ethics, historical inequality and public economics. Research Methods & Statistics and qualitative inquiry provide different empirical methods. The two plans each add ten different courses and have distinct academic priorities. The historical research seminar and Social Movements & Environmental Justice receive substantive weight for historical inquiry and mobilisation respectively within what their descriptions support. Negotiation and simulated arbitration add real practice but do not sustain a third legal route; much of the law and advocacy core would repeat the closest option. The Madrid dual degree is confirmed but has no defensible counterpart in these courses.

candidateDecisions.label: Law and contemporary social problems: human rights, criminal justice, inequality and social movements
Negotiation, mediation, dispute resolution and moot-court advocacy
candidateDecisions.reason: Principles of Private Law includes simulated mediation and negotiation. Criminal Law & Criminal Justice includes simulated legal advice and oral argument. Rhetoric, negotiation, business law and peace studies add complementary practice. The closest option already contains much of this core. The remaining coursework would shift towards business or political conflict and would lack sustained legal mediation, procedure and advocacy.

candidateDecisions.label: Spanish law and the Spanish and European law dual degree
candidateDecisions.reason: Annex 4a confirms a selective four-year Madrid dual degree. UCR does not provide Spanish law or the prescribed partner-university sequence.

alignment.rationale: Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Foundations of Law teaches legal history, legal philosophy and law and economics as the foundations of positive law; UCR has no jurisprudence or legal-history course, and Ethics, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Modern History and Introduction to Economics contribute related perspectives without directly addressing the legal-historical, legal-philosophical or economic-analysis-of-law content of the component.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Philosophy of Private Law applies normative theories of justice to private-law doctrines; Ethics teaches the general normative theories but no UCR course addresses private-law doctrine from a philosophical standpoint, so the relationship is contextual.

Comparative Constitutional Law covers the institutions of government, limits on government power, guarantees of rights and judicial review across five legal systems, the subject of Constitutional Law; it is narrower on European and international constitutionalism and adds administrative law.

Introduction to Public International Law covers the sources, subjects and organisation of international law, the use of force and treaty compliance, the international-law half of International and European Law; the EU half is aligned separately with Law of the European Union.

Foundations of European Union Law covers the EU institutional framework, legal order, fundamental rights, citizenship and free movement, the subject of Law of the European Union at a more introductory level.
Comparative Constitutional Law introduces administrative decision-making, judicial review, remedies and procedural fairness. Maastricht develops administrative law in a dedicated second-year course.
Principles of Private Law covers property, tort and contract law comparatively across several legal systems, the subject of Introduction to Private Law (family law is not named in its description).
The UCR private-law course covers comparative property, tort and contract law. Maastricht develops private law over two compulsory courses.
Criminal Law & Criminal Justice covers criminal accountability, the legality principle, justifications and excuses and the justification of punishment, the subject of Criminal Law.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Criminal Procedure covers investigative measures, pre-trial detention, prosecution and the criminal trial from a comparative perspective; Criminal Law & Criminal Justice is already the counterpart to Criminal Law and does not teach criminal procedure.
Peace & Conflict supplies conflict analysis and peacebuilding. UCR also practises mediation in private law, but has no equivalent dedicated legal conflict-resolution and advocacy sequence.

Both develop introductory legal reasoning and case analysis. UCR uses case briefs, interpretation, demand letters and mock trials. Maastricht teaches legal sources and drafting in a dedicated skills sequence.

The Art of Rhetorical Communication teaches the theory of rhetoric and argumentation, which corresponds to the legal-argumentation part of Thinking Like a Lawyer (structure and evaluation of arguments, persuasion); it does not teach legal syllogisms, the legal challenge or legal reasoning and covers only part of the component's scope.

Maastricht teaches legal research methodology and writing in a dedicated course. UCR develops case-law research in its law courses and offers separate historical, qualitative and empirical research training.
Maastricht requires an individual legal paper, public defence and final portfolio. UCR displays optional independent research alongside it.
The 48 EC elective phase follows a learning plan and includes limits on non-law, introductory and internship credits. The exact selection is left open.
